title: Markets: Saturday 31 October

morning.session_note: Weekend edition · the week in review, with the week ahead
summary: Doubts about whether heavy AI spending will pay off hit US tech this week: the Nasdaq fell 2.0% for the week and the S&P 500 0.6%, after Alphabet's largest one-day fall on record on Thursday and a 29% drop in Intel on Friday, its worst day since the 1970s ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/amazon-intel-earnings-big-tech-ai-spending-concerns.html)). The US 10-year yield ended the week at 4.94%, 6 bp lower.

Australian inflation rose to 4.3% in September and the quarterly trimmed mean rose 1.0%, above the RBA's 0.8% forecast, so all four major banks now expect a hike on Tuesday ([ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/cpi-rose-43-year-september-2026), [AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/the-figures-to-watch-ahead-of-melbourne-cup-rate-call)). ASX futures put the chance at 78% at Friday's close ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). The Fed held, with two officials voting to hike ([Federal Reserve](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm)).

Brent rose 13.6% in October, according to Reuters, as the US weighed new strikes on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections and a tanker in Hormuz was hit by limpet mines ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/oil-rises-on-supply-concerns-as-houthis-attack-saudi-arabia.html), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/us-iran-war-oil-prices-strait-hormuz-10-30-26)). Iran has received a US letter on talks but had not replied as of Thursday, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim agency ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-diplomacy-threat-resume-attacks/)).

cards.headline: AI spending doubts pulled the Nasdaq down 2.0% for the week
cards.takeaway: Alphabet, Intel and Amazon fell after results, while energy, financials, utilities and healthcare were set for monthly gains.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Alphabet's fall was covered in the 30 Oct issue. Friday's Intel and chip selloff and the weekly totals are new.
cards.what_happened: Alphabet fell 12.6% on Thursday, its largest one-day fall on record, after search revenue missed forecasts and free cash flow was −US$9.1 billion ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october)). On Friday Intel fell 29%, its worst day since the 1970s, after weaker-than-expected guidance citing a plant shutdown in Israel and PC softness; Nvidia fell 4%, Broadcom more than 5% and Qualcomm 11%, while Amazon slipped 1.4% after a third-quarter miss and kept its 2026 capex forecast at US$220 billion ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/amazon-intel-earnings-big-tech-ai-spending-concerns.html)). Microsoft drew more than US$100 billion of orders for a US$25 billion bond sale ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october)).
cards.why_it_matters: The question has moved from whether AI demand is real to how the spending is funded: Alphabet and Meta are now burning cash while Microsoft is borrowing ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october)). Profits are still strong, with S&P 500 third-quarter earnings on pace to rise 31% according to LSEG data, and energy, financials, utilities and healthcare were set for monthly gains ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/midterm-elections-earnings-jobs-data-loom-for-aiwary-market-4986533)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: S&P 500 7,580.1 (−1.8% day, −0.6% week), Nasdaq 25,437.0 (−2.9% day, −2.0% week), VIX 19.45 (+2.25 points day, unchanged for the week).

competing_views.view: Said the concern is not slowing AI demand but that "higher funding costs and credit risk could eventually force hyperscalers to slow their build-out".
"The market is much more broad than people generally want to give it credit for."

cards.what_to_watch: Apple reports on Monday US time (Tuesday morning Sydney), with AMD, Qualcomm and Palantir also due next week.

cards.headline: The Fed held as US growth beat forecasts and inflation rose
cards.takeaway: Two Fed officials voted for a hike, and analysts are split on whether December's expected rise is the last.
cards.key_figure: US Q3 GDP: +3.4% annualised; September PCE inflation 3.6% y/y
cards.new_since_last_issue: The Fed decision and GDP were covered on 29 and 30 Oct. The wage data and analysts' views on the path are new.
cards.what_happened: The Fed held its range at 3.75–4.00% on a 10–2 vote, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack preferring a 25 bp hike, and said economic activity is expanding "at a strong pace" ([Federal Reserve](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm)). Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, up from 2.2% ([BEA](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-3rd-quarter-2026)). September PCE prices rose 0.5% in the month and 3.6% from a year earlier, with core at 3.1% ([BEA](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-september-2026)). Employment costs rose 0.8% in the quarter and 3.4% over the year ([BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/eci.nr0.htm)).
cards.why_it_matters: Wages and salaries rose 3.1% over the year, and the BLS said inflation-adjusted wages fell 0.6% ([BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/eci.nr0.htm)). The Fed's statement said inflation "remains elevated", and two officials voted to hike ([Federal Reserve](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm)).

competing_views.who: Kay Haigh, Goldman Sachs Asset Management
competing_views.view: Said the Fed's pause will likely be short-lived and expects hikes to resume in December, with more tightening possible next year if energy prices rise again.
Expects a final 25 bp hike in December, then easing from mid-2027 as core PCE falls to about 2.5% by end-2027.

cards.what_to_watch: October payrolls on Friday US time (Saturday Sydney); consensus is 55,000 jobs and 4.2% unemployment, according to Newsquawk.

cards.headline: ASX 200 rose 1.3% for the week as Coles slumped
cards.takeaway: Healthcare and a Zip rebound lifted the index, while Coles guided to flat first-half supermarket earnings.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Coles and Catalyst were covered on 30 Oct. The weekly picture is new.
cards.what_happened: Coles fell more than 12% during Friday's session after guiding to flat first-half supermarket earnings of about A$1.23 billion, about 7% below UBS's forecast. Catalyst Metals fell 22%. Consumer discretionary was down about 2% for the week, while healthcare has risen 38% since late July ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october)).
cards.why_it_matters: Coles cited price investment, competitor promotions and higher fuel costs for the flat outlook. Westpac reports on Monday, NAB on Thursday and Macquarie on Friday, ahead of Tuesday's RBA decision ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: ASX 200 8,908.1 (+0.2% day, +1.3% week); AUD/USD 0.7040 (−0.2% day, +0.5% week). ASX 200 futures and iron ore are unavailable in our data.

cards.headline: Hot inflation made a Melbourne Cup Day rate hike the base case
cards.takeaway: Core inflation beat the RBA's forecast, and all four major banks now expect a rise to 4.85% on Tuesday.
cards.key_figure: Trimmed mean: +1.0% q/q, 3.7% y/y (RBA forecast 0.8% q/q)
cards.new_since_last_issue: The CPI was covered on 28 Oct. Friday's closing odds and the RBA's response are new.
cards.what_happened: CPI rose 4.3% in the year to September, up from 4.0%, with fuel up 9.4% in the month ([ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/cpi-rose-43-year-september-2026)). The quarterly trimmed mean rose 1.0%, above the RBA's 0.8% forecast, and NAB and CBA moved to forecast a hike, joining ANZ and Westpac ([AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/the-figures-to-watch-ahead-of-melbourne-cup-rate-call)). ASX futures implied a 78% chance of a hike at Friday's close, up from 56% a week earlier ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)).
cards.why_it_matters: Housing rose 5.2% and transport 8.7% over the year, so the pressure is not only fuel ([ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/cpi-rose-43-year-september-2026)). Treasurer Chalmers has promised savings in December's mid-year budget update, while the Opposition's Tim Wilson said government spending is forcing the RBA's hand ([AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/the-figures-to-watch-ahead-of-melbourne-cup-rate-call)). The RBA publishes new forecasts on the same day as the decision.

competing_views.view: "This is an ugly number for the RBA and significantly strengthens the case for another rate hike next week."
Said inflation was too high but broadly in line with what the RBA had expected.

cards.what_to_watch: The decision and Statement on Monetary Policy at 2:30pm Sydney time on Tuesday, then Governor Bullock's media conference at 3:30pm.

cards.headline: US yields fell for the week while Australia's short end rose
cards.takeaway: The US 2-year yield fell 13 bp for the week, while Australia's 2-year rose 3 bp as RBA hike odds climbed.
cards.key_figure: US 2Y 4.56% (−13 bp week); AU 2Y 4.95% (+3 bp week)
cards.what_happened: The US 10-year yield ended the week 6 bp lower at 4.94% and the 2-year 13 bp lower at 4.56%, according to our data. CNBC put the 30-year at 5.31% on Friday ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/us-treasury-yields-fed-interest-rates.html)). In Australia, the RBA's latest published data, for 28 October, show the 10-year at 5.21%, 7 bp lower than a week earlier, and the 2-year at 4.95%, 3 bp higher, leaving the 10-year 26 bp above the 2-year.
cards.why_it_matters: In Australia, ASX futures moved from 56% to 78% odds of a November hike over the week ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). The US Treasury's quarterly refunding on Wednesday will show whether it changes coupon auction sizes, which matters for long-end yields ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: US 10Y 4.94% (−4 bp day, −6 bp week); US 2Y 4.56% (−5 bp day, −13 bp week); AU 10Y 5.21% and AU 2Y 4.95% as at 28 Oct (RBA, lagged).
cards.what_to_watch: US Treasury refunding announcement on Wednesday US time; RBA decision on Tuesday.

cards.headline: Central banks split between holding and hiking on energy inflation
cards.takeaway: The ECB, BoJ and RBNZ held while Canada hiked, and Lagarde will leave the ECB early.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Each decision was covered in this week's daily issues; this card pulls them together.
cards.what_happened: The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5%, and Christine Lagarde will step down on 7 February 2027 ([ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr261029~abbb6dc64b.en.html), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/29/ecb-holds-rates-at-25-as-lagarde-announces-early-exit-with-inflation-near-double-the-targe)). The BoJ held at 1.25% in an 8–1 vote, the Bank of Canada raised rates by 25 bp, and the RBNZ held at 2.75% on a 4–3 vote when markets had priced about a 93% chance of a hike. Italy's flash inflation reached 5.6% ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)).
cards.why_it_matters: The Bank of England is expected to begin hiking with a 25 bp rise on Thursday, according to Newsquawk. The ECB said it is "not pre-committing to a particular rate path" (Euronews). The RBNZ held on a 4–3 vote when money markets had priced about a 93% chance of a hike (Newsquawk).

cards.headline: The US weighed post-midterm strikes on Iran as mediators pushed for talks
cards.takeaway: Trump says the war will end soon, Tehran had not answered a US letter as of Thursday, and military options are on the table for after 3 November.
cards.new_since_last_issue: The Vance letter was covered on 29 and 30 Oct. Friday's statements, the mediation and the briefing on strike options are new.
cards.what_happened: Defense Secretary Hegseth, Gen. Caine and Adm. Cooper briefed Trump on military options for after the midterms, the WSJ reported ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/us-iran-war-oil-prices-strait-hormuz-10-30-26)). Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday, and the NYT reported joint US-Israeli strike planning for after 3 November ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/30/us-weighs-new-iran-strikes-as-vance-reaches-out-is-war-or-a-deal-closer)). Vice President Vance's letter says talks "require discussions on the nuclear issue" ([Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/28/vance-iran-nuclear-talks-letter)), and the Guardian reported it sets out a seven-day process to reopen Hormuz in return for sanctions relief ([Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/29/jd-vance-letter-may-offer-last-chance-to-avert-fresh-conflict-between-us-and-iran)).
cards.why_it_matters: Fuel was the main driver of Australia's September inflation, according to the Treasurer ([AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/the-figures-to-watch-ahead-of-melbourne-cup-rate-call)), so the outcome of talks bears on the RBA. Saxo Bank expects oil volatility around the 3 November midterms ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/oil-rises-on-supply-concerns-as-houthis-attack-saudi-arabia.html)). Pakistan, another mediator, said it is "cautiously optimistic" ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/us-iran-war-oil-prices-strait-hormuz-10-30-26)).

competing_views.view: "One way or the other, it's going to end very soon," he said on Friday, adding that Iran "wants to talk".
Said Iran's conditions for talks are unchanged, including lifting the blockade, sanctions relief and access to frozen assets.

cards.what_to_watch: Any Iranian reply to the letter, and statements from Washington in the days after Tuesday's vote.

cards.headline: Brent rose 13.6% in October as Hormuz attacks continued
cards.takeaway: A limpet-mine attack in Hormuz and Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi sites lifted oil, though the December contract's expiry muddies the weekly figure.
cards.key_figure: January Brent settle US$113.43 (+US$2.63); Brent +13.6% in October
cards.what_happened: The expiring December Brent contract settled up 2.4% at US$117.64 on Friday and the more active January contract rose US$2.63 to US$113.43; WTI settled at US$104.12 ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/oil-rises-on-supply-concerns-as-houthis-attack-saudi-arabia.html)). A tanker in the strait was hit by limpet mines, the first known successful limpet-mine strike in the waterway since the war began, maritime sources told CNBC, and UKMTO data showed October had the most incidents since the conflict began ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/us-iran-war-oil-prices-strait-hormuz-10-30-26)).
cards.why_it_matters: Supply is still moving: Adm. Cooper said the primary transit routes are clear and Gulf partners have exported more than 1.5 billion barrels with US help since summer ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/us-iran-war-oil-prices-strait-hormuz-10-30-26)), and Saudi exports rose in October ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/oil-rises-on-supply-concerns-as-houthis-attack-saudi-arabia.html)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: Brent futures 112.42 (−2.1% day, −3.7% week; Yahoo feed, see comparison below); Brent spot 123.10 as at 27 Oct (FRED, lagged), +6.8% on the prior week.

competing_views.who: Adm. Brad Cooper, US Central Command
competing_views.view: Said the primary transit routes through Hormuz have been cleared of mines and Iran's navy "is all at the bottom of the sea".
Expects crude to trade in a US$70–90 range even after the conflict ends, above the pre-war US$60–70 range.

comparison.title: Which Brent price for Friday?
comparison.why_different: December Brent expired on Friday. Our Yahoo BZ=F feed appears to have rolled to the January contract, so its −2.1% compares a January price with Thursday's December settle of 114.88, and its −3.7% weekly change compares it with last Friday's December settle. Reported settles show both contracts rose on Friday. A gap of about US$1 between the feed and the reported January settle remains, possibly from a different close time; we have not confirmed this.

rows.measure: Brent front-month financial futures, daily close

cards.what_to_watch: Tanker incidents in Hormuz and Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities, especially around Tuesday's US election.

cards.headline: Wall Street expects Democratic gains in Tuesday's midterms
cards.takeaway: A Democratic House is the consensus, the Senate is closer, and analysts disagree on what a sweep means for AI stocks and bonds.
cards.what_happened: Polymarket odds give Democrats a 94% chance of the House and 69% of the Senate, according to Newsquawk ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)). Wolfe Research puts the chance of a Democratic Senate at 49%, and Piper Sandler estimates Democratic proposals would add US$5 trillion to deficits over a decade ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/2026-midterm-election-wall-street-prepares-for-democratic-gains.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Investors are watching data-centre policy, including state and local races in Texas, plus defence, healthcare and bank regulation ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/midterm-elections-earnings-jobs-data-loom-for-aiwary-market-4986533)). The US is expected to reach its debt limit in 2027, so control of Congress also shapes that fight ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/2026-midterm-election-wall-street-prepares-for-democratic-gains.html)).

competing_views.view: Said a significant blue wave would likely be seen as negative for AI names, tech in general "and maybe even for the market as a whole".
Said a Democratic Senate could ease concerns about Fed independence, because new Fed members need Senate confirmation.

cards.what_to_watch: Results arrive from Wednesday morning Sydney time; a slow or contested count is a risk analysts flag.

cards.headline: Gold fell to a one-year low as a crypto hack added to selling
cards.takeaway: Gold and silver dropped despite war risk as rate-hike expectations rose, while a suspected Binance hack hit Bitcoin.
cards.key_figure: Spot gold US$3,880 (−3.5% Friday), lowest since 6 Oct 2025
cards.what_happened: Spot gold fell 3.5% to about US$3,880 on Friday and spot silver fell to US$48.95, Kitco reported, citing higher oil prices feeding expectations of further Fed hikes ([Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-10-30/gold-prices-plunge-one-year-low-below-3900-higher-oil-prices-fuel-fears)). Binance suspended deposits and withdrawals over a suspected hack with about US$3 billion of assets frozen, and Bitcoin fell below US$77,000 ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-friday-30th-october)).
cards.why_it_matters: Analysts quoted by Kitco said gold fell even as the dollar and bond yields weakened, and that it is reacting to inflation expectations and the future path of interest rates ([Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-10-30/gold-prices-plunge-one-year-low-below-3900-higher-oil-prices-fuel-fears)).

rba.summary: ASX 30-day interbank futures implied a 78% chance of a 25 bp hike on 3 November at Friday's close (expected rate 4.79%), up from 56% a week earlier.

forecasts.view: All four expect a hike in November, after NAB and CBA switched from a hold following the CPI.
Said the RBA may need unemployment nearer 5.5% than 5% to bring inflation down, which would require tighter financial conditions.

fed.summary: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00%; December hike bets fell to 76% after Thursday's PCE and GDP data, according to Market Index.

forecasts.who: Kay Haigh, Goldman Sachs Asset Management
forecasts.view: Expects hikes to resume in December.
Expects a final 25 bp hike in December, then easing from mid-2027.

watchlist.note: Rose 22.6% for the week to A$1.79, recovering part of the previous Friday's 29% plunge on US fraud losses. Monday's 14% jump came as UBS called the selloff "an overreaction" and Macquarie kept its A$3.50 target, while Citi and Jefferies were more cautious. It slipped 3.8% on Friday. ASX filings show MUFG became a substantial holder on 28 October and ceased to be one on 30 October, and three directors lodged interest-change notices.

Rose 2.0% for the week to A$200.73, helped by a broad healthcare rally that has lifted the sector 38% since late July. CSL held its AGM on Tuesday, said Brian McNamee will retire with Gordon Naylor as the next chair, and kept buying back shares.

Rose 0.9% for the week to A$11.35, with no company announcements since 20 October. It moved with the consumer discretionary sector, which snapped a four-day losing streak on Friday but was still down about 2% for the week, according to Market Index.
watchlist.next_catalyst: Tuesday's RBA decision, which affects household travel budgets.

watchlist.note: Unchanged for the week at A$2.21 (−0.5% Friday). The company kept buying back shares, a substantial holder exited on 28 October and final director's interest notices were lodged for A Barker and A Barkla on 29 October; none of these filings was marked price-sensitive, and no report we found explains the week's moves.
